main_body: Snow-laden conifer: a tiered cone of dark green boughs with white snow caps on each tier, a short brown trunk and a snow base
top_band: Down the centre column: white/pale-blue snow cap at rows 1-3, then green bough. Snow bands of about 3-4 rows follow at rows 12-14, 23-26, 34-37 and 45-49, each sitting above a green boughs face
evidence: Each tier has a snow band several rows thick, lighter than the foliage, which reads as a horizontal surface seen from above. Below each band the boughs form a darker front face, and the drooping snow edges shade the boughs under them. This is an organic canopy, not a flat elevation, and it has no receding side faces. The bands are irregular and there is no crisp front-edge line, but the main body clearly shows both top surfaces and front faces.

style.evidence: The foliage uses about four or five greens, from dark teal-green to a mid green highlight, plus three snow tones. The outline is a tinted dark green rather than neutral black, and it is used selectively. The boughs have clumped, jagged edges, and the snow has per-tier shading and drips. The tree is smaller and less leafy than the broadleaf references, but it has no large flat fills and would sit acceptably beside them.
